diagnosis: I calibrated the model with a global search method (DDS) on 1971-10 to 1997-12, after a one-year warm-up, targeting daily NSE. This used about 5,500 model runs. The fit is NSE 0.86, KGE 0.88 and r 0.93. Simulated flow is about 6% too high overall (PBIAS +5.7%). A second search from a different starting seed only moved NSE from 0.8624 to 0.8625, so the optimum looks stable for this model structure. Parameters: FC about 210 mm, LP 0.57, BETA 1.5, K1 0.33, K2 0.10, PERC 1.6, UZL 42 and MAXBAS 3.5 days, which is reasonable for a large lowland catchment. Snow matters little (about 3% of precipitation falls as snow), so the snow parameters (TT, CFMAX, CFR, CWH) are poorly identified; CWH ended at its lower limit, which has negligible effect. Likely weaknesses: the timing and size of the highest winter floods, which are dampened by six upstream reservoirs and the floodplain; low flows in late summer, which are affected by reservoir releases and abstraction; and a tendency to produce slightly too much water. I did not test the parameters on a held-out part of the record. Confidence is moderate to high: the parameters are physically plausible, and NSE in an independent period would probably be around 0.80–0.86.
